name: Holographic QCD and confinement
summary: Confinement maps to a bulk geometry that caps off: in Witten's model the confinement-deconfinement transition is the Hawking-Page transition, Wilson loops are minimal string worldsheets with area law, and AdS/QCD models fit Regge trajectories.
breaks: QCD is not conformal in the UV, has N=3 and no supersymmetry; holographic QCD lacks asymptotic freedom and has no known exact string dual.
sources: Witten (1998). "Anti-de Sitter space, thermal phase transition, and confinement in gauge theories". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 505. [arXiv:hep-th/9803131](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803131)
Maldacena (1998). "Wilson loops in large N field theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 4859. [arXiv:hep-th/9803002](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803002)

name: Spin networks are gauge-invariant Wilson-loop states
summary: Ashtekar variables make GR an SU(2) connection theory; LQG states are holonomies (Wilson lines) on graphs labelled by spins, the same gauge-invariant basis used in Hamiltonian (Kogut-Susskind) lattice gauge theory, but on graphs that are not embedded in a fixed metric.
sources: Rovelli & Smolin (1990). "Loop space representation of quantum general relativity". *Nucl. Phys. B* 331, 80. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(90)90019-A](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(90)90019-A)

name: CDT: lattice Monte Carlo for spacetime
summary: Causal dynamical triangulations regularize the gravitational path integral on simplicial lattices, sample it by Monte Carlo after Wick rotation, and seek a continuum limit at a second-order transition, the lattice-QCD strategy applied to geometry; a 4D de Sitter-like phase emerges.
map: Z=\sum_T\frac{1}{C_T}e^{-S_{\rm Regge}[T]}\ \leftrightarrow\ Z=\int\mathcal DU\,e^{-S_W[U]};\ \text{continuum limit at a 2nd-order point}
sources: Loll (2020). "Quantum Gravity from Causal Dynamical Triangulations: A Review". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 37, 013002. [arXiv:1905.08669](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08669)

name: Asymptotic safety: a UV fixed point for gravity
summary: Wilsonian and functional RG methods from QFT show evidence that Newton's dimensionless coupling g=Gk^2 flows to a non-Gaussian UV fixed point, making gravity non-perturbatively renormalizable, the gravitational analogue of asymptotic freedom with a non-zero fixed point.
sources: Niedermaier & Reuter (2006). "The Asymptotic Safety Scenario in Quantum Gravity". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 9, 5. [doi:10.12942/lrr-2006-5](https://doi.org/10.12942/lrr-2006-5)

name: Asymptotic safety predicted the Higgs mass
summary: Requiring the SM plus gravity to be asymptotically safe forces the Higgs quartic near zero at the Planck scale, predicting m_h of about 126 GeV with a few-GeV uncertainty two years before the 125 GeV discovery.
breaks: The prediction depends on assumed signs of gravitational anomalous dimensions; it is the same boundary condition as near-criticality of the SM vacuum and is not unique to asymptotic safety.
sources: Shaposhnikov & Wetterich (2010). "Asymptotic safety of gravity and the Higgs boson mass". *Phys. Lett. B* 683, 196. [arXiv:0912.0208](https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.0208)

name: Trace and gravitational anomalies fix Hawking flux
summary: Regularization breaks classical conformal and diffeomorphism symmetry just as it breaks axial symmetry (ABJ): the trace anomaly sources <T_mu^mu> in curved space, and demanding cancellation of the near-horizon gravitational anomaly reproduces the Hawking flux.
sources: Robinson & Wilczek (2005). "Relationship between Hawking Radiation and Gravitational Anomalies". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 011303. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502074](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502074)

name: Bogoliubov transformations and vacuum ambiguity
summary: Canonical field quantization carries over to curved spacetime, but without a global timelike Killing vector the mode split into positive and negative frequency is not unique; in- and out-vacua related by Bogoliubov coefficients give particle creation (cosmological, Hawking, Unruh).
sources: Parker (1969). "Quantized Fields and Particle Creation in Expanding Universes. I". *Phys. Rev.* 183, 1057. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.183.1057](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.183.1057)

name: Higgs vacuum metastability in curved spacetime
summary: With m_h=125 GeV and m_t=173 GeV the Higgs quartic runs negative near 1e10-1e11 GeV, so the electroweak vacuum is metastable; gravitational corrections to the bounce (Coleman-De Luccia) and Higgs fluctuations during inflation decide whether our vacuum survives.
sources: Coleman & De Luccia (1980). "Gravitational effects on and of vacuum decay". *Phys. Rev. D* 21, 3305. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.21.3305](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.21.3305)
Degrassi et al. (2012). "Higgs mass and vacuum stability in the Standard Model at NNLO". *JHEP* 08, 098. [arXiv:1205.6497](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.6497)

name: String compactifications as BSM model building
summary: Calabi-Yau, orbifold and brane-world compactifications generate gauge groups, chiral matter, axions, moduli and hidden sectors; BSM phenomenology inherits candidates (axiverse, moduli, GUT-like groups) and constraints (swampland conjectures) from string vacua.
breaks: The landscape of vacua is so large that few sharp low-energy predictions follow; no compactification uniquely reproduces the SM.
sources: Arvanitaki et al. (2010). "String Axiverse". *Phys. Rev. D* 81, 123530. [arXiv:0905.4720](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.4720)

name: Compactified dimensions and the hierarchy problem
summary: String theory needs six extra dimensions; large (ADD) or warped (Randall-Sundrum) extra dimensions lower the fundamental gravity scale to TeV, and the RS warp factor is a slice of AdS5, so hierarchy models and holography share one geometry.
map: M_{\rm Pl}^2\simeq M_*^{n+2}R^n\ (\text{ADD}),\qquad m_{\rm TeV}=e^{-kr_c\pi}M_{\rm Pl}\ (\text{RS, AdS}_5\ \text{slice})
sources: Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos & Dvali (1998). "The Hierarchy problem and new dimensions at a millimeter". *Phys. Lett. B* 429, 263. [arXiv:hep-ph/9803315](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9803315)
Randall & Sundrum (1999). "A Large Mass Hierarchy from a Small Extra Dimension". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 83, 3370. [arXiv:hep-ph/9905221](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9905221)

name: Superstrings require supersymmetry
summary: Removing the bosonic-string tachyon and including fermions requires worldsheet supersymmetry, which with GSO projection yields spacetime supersymmetry; superstring compactifications are the main UV source of SUSY and supergravity model building.
breaks: Low-scale (TeV) SUSY is not predicted by string theory; the SUSY-breaking scale is unconstrained and LHC has not seen superpartners.
sources: Green & Schwarz (1984). "Anomaly cancellations in supersymmetric D = 10 gauge theory and superstring theory". *Phys. Lett. B* 149, 117. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(84)91565-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(84)91565-X)

name: Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation
summary: The same consistency principle that fixes SM hypercharges (gauge anomaly cancellation) fixes superstring gauge groups: gauge and gravitational anomalies of 10D supergravity cancel only for SO(32) or E8xE8 via the Green-Schwarz counterterm.
sources: Green & Schwarz (1984). "Anomaly cancellations in supersymmetric D = 10 gauge theory and superstring theory". *Phys. Lett. B* 149, 117. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(84)91565-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(84)91565-X)

name: D-brane open strings give Yang-Mills
summary: The massless modes of open strings ending on N coincident D-branes are a U(N) gauge field plus adjoint scalars; their low-energy action is (super) Yang-Mills, so gauge theories arise as brane worldvolume theories, the starting point of AdS/CFT and brane-world model building.
sources: Polchinski (1995). "Dirichlet Branes and Ramond-Ramond Charges". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 4724. [arXiv:hep-th/9510017](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9510017)
Witten (1996). "Bound states of strings and p-branes". *Nucl. Phys. B* 460, 335. [arXiv:hep-th/9510135](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9510135)

name: String theory born from hadron Regge trajectories
summary: The Veneziano amplitude was invented to fit linearly rising Regge trajectories of mesons; reinterpreted as vibrating strings, it predicted a massless spin-2 state that became the graviton once QCD took over the strong interaction.
sources: Veneziano (1968). "Construction of a crossing-symmetric, Regge-behaved amplitude for linearly rising trajectories". *Nuovo Cimento A* 57, 190. [doi:10.1007/BF02824451](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02824451)

name: Large-N planar diagrams equal string genus expansion
summary: In 't Hooft's large-N limit Feynman diagrams of SU(N) gauge theory organize by the genus of the surface they tile, weighted N^(2-2g), the same topological expansion as closed-string perturbation theory with g_s ~ 1/N; this is the structural root of gauge/string duality.
sources: 't Hooft (1974). "A planar diagram theory for strong interactions". *Nucl. Phys. B* 72, 461. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(74)90154-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(74)90154-0)

name: Particles as unitary irreps of the Poincare group
summary: Wigner's classification defines an elementary particle as an irreducible unitary representation of the Poincare group, labelled by mass and spin (or helicity for m=0); spinor-helicity and little-group scaling in modern amplitudes are the same construction.
map: P^\mu P_\mu=-m^2c^2,\ W^\mu W_\mu=m^2c^2\hbar^2s(s+1);\quad m=0:\ \text{little group }ISO(2)\Rightarrow h=\pm s
sources: Wigner (1939). "On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group". *Ann. Math.* 40, 149. [doi:10.2307/1968551](https://doi.org/10.2307/1968551)

name: Invariant mass and collider kinematics
summary: Collider physics runs on four-momentum invariants: resonance discovery by invariant-mass peaks, sqrt(s) of colliding beams versus fixed targets, rapidity and transverse momentum as boost-friendly variables, and partonic s-hat = x1 x2 s.

name: Muon storage rings test time dilation
summary: The muon g-2 storage ring runs at the magic gamma=29.3, where the Thomas-BMT spin precession decouples from electric focusing; the dilated muon lifetime there confirmed SR time dilation to about 1e-3.
sources: Bailey et al. (1977). "Measurements of relativistic time dilatation for positive and negative muons in a circular orbit". *Nature* 268, 301. [doi:10.1038/268301a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/268301a0)

name: Neutrino speed bounds and the OPERA error
summary: Neutrino time of flight from SN1987A and long-baseline beams bounds |v-c|/c; the 2011 OPERA superluminal claim was traced to a faulty fibre connection, and superluminal neutrinos would lose energy by e+e- pair emission.
sources: Cohen & Glashow (2011). "Pair Creation Constrains Superluminal Neutrino Propagation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 107, 181803. [arXiv:1109.6562](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.6562)

name: Standard-Model Extension as an EFT of Lorentz violation
summary: The SME adds every Lorentz-violating operator built from SM fields contracted with fixed background tensors (a_mu, b_mu, c_munu, ...), turning clock, cavity, meson and astrophysical tests into bounds on a common coefficient table.
sources: Colladay & Kostelecky (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [arXiv:hep-ph/9809521](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9809521)
Kostelecky & Russell (2011). "Data Tables for Lorentz and CPT Violation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 11. [arXiv:0801.0287](https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.0287)

name: CPT violation requires Lorentz violation
summary: In an interacting unitary QFT, CPT violation implies Lorentz violation, so neutral-kaon and B-meson CPT interferometry bound the CPT-odd SME coefficients a_mu with sidereal-time modulation.
sources: Greenberg (2002). "CPT Violation Implies Violation of Lorentz Invariance". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 89, 231602. [arXiv:hep-ph/0201258](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0201258)

name: Peccei-Quinn axion couples through the QCD anomaly
summary: The axion is the pseudo-Goldstone boson of an anomalous U(1)_PQ. The anomaly couples it to G G-tilde exactly like the theta term, so its instanton-generated potential relaxes the effective theta-bar to zero. Its photon coupling is likewise fixed by the electromagnetic anomaly coefficient E/N.

name: Strong CP problem and axion mass from QCD topology
summary: QCD allows a CP-violating theta-bar = theta + arg det M_q, and the neutron EDM bound forces |theta-bar| below about 1e-10: the strong CP problem the axion solves. The axion mass is set by QCD's topological susceptibility, m_a^2 f_a^2 = chi_top, and lattice results for chi_top(T) fix the axion relic abundance from misalignment.
map: \bar\theta=\theta+\arg\det M_q\lesssim10^{-10};\ m_a^2f_a^2=\chi_{\rm top},\ m_a\approx5.7\,\mu{\rm eV}\left(\frac{10^{12}\,{\rm GeV}}{f_a}\right)

name: Leptogenesis and Majorana neutrino mass
summary: In thermal leptogenesis, the heavy Majorana neutrinos of the seesaw decay CP-asymmetrically and sphalerons convert the resulting lepton asymmetry into baryons. Seeing neutrinoless double-beta decay would establish the lepton-number violation and Majorana nature leptogenesis needs, but would not fix its high-scale CP phases.

name: Sphalerons: B+L violation from the electroweak anomaly
summary: Through the SU(2) anomaly, baryon and lepton number change whenever the Chern-Simons number changes ('t Hooft). Tunneling is negligible today, but thermal sphalerons are fast above the electroweak scale. They supply Sakharov's B violation and convert lepton asymmetries into baryons while conserving B-L.
map: \partial_\mu j_B^\mu=\partial_\mu j_L^\mu=\frac{N_f}{32\pi^2}\left(g^2W\tilde W-g'^2B\tilde B\right),\ \Delta B=\Delta L=N_f\Delta N_{CS}

name: CKM CP violation is too weak for the baryon asymmetry
summary: Sakharov's second condition needs C and CP violation. The CKM phase provides it, but at the electroweak scale its effect is suppressed by the Jarlskog invariant times quark-mass differences to about 1e-20, far below eta_B of about 6e-10, so a new CP-violating source is required.
sources: Sakharov (1967; reprinted 1991). "Violation of CP invariance, C asymmetry, and baryon asymmetry of the universe". *Sov. Phys. Usp.* 34, 392. [doi:10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497](https://doi.org/10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497)

name: Electroweak phase transition and baryogenesis
summary: Electroweak baryogenesis needs a strongly first-order transition, so that sphalerons switch off inside expanding bubbles. Lattice studies show the SM transition is a smooth crossover (near 160 GeV) for m_h above about 70 GeV. A 125 GeV Higgs therefore rules out SM electroweak baryogenesis and points to extended scalar sectors that colliders can test.

name: keV sterile neutrinos as warm dark matter
summary: A keV-mass gauge-singlet neutrino produced by oscillations (Dodelson-Widrow) or resonantly is a warm dark-matter candidate. X-ray searches for nu_s -> nu gamma and small-scale structure constrain it, and the 3.5 keV line claim is contested and unconfirmed. The eV-scale steriles invoked for the short-baseline anomalies are a separate mass range.

name: Warped extra dimension dual to a composite-Higgs CFT
summary: By the AdS/CFT dictionary, a Randall-Sundrum slice of AdS5 with an IR brane is dual to a strongly coupled, nearly conformal 4D theory that confines at the TeV scale. KK modes map to composite resonances, the IR-brane Higgs to a composite Higgs, and the warp factor to the RG scale (Arkani-Hamed-Porrati-Randall 2001).
map: z\leftrightarrow1/\mu,\ \text{IR brane}\leftrightarrow\Lambda_{\rm comp}\sim{\rm TeV},\ m_{\rm KK}\leftrightarrow m_\rho,\ \Delta=2+\sqrt{4+m^2L^2}
breaks: The duality is derived only for large-N theories with string duals such as N=4 SYM. The CFT dual to a phenomenological RS model is not known explicitly, so the map is a heuristic dictionary.

name: Hierarchy problem: the unprotected Higgs mass
summary: The Higgs mass term is the SM's only relevant operator and no symmetry protects it, so heavy thresholds feed into m_H^2. Large and warped extra dimensions, compositeness and SUSY are the proposed cures, and LHC null results sharpen the puzzle into the little hierarchy problem.
breaks: In dimensional regularization no Lambda^2 appears; the physical issue is sensitivity to the masses of heavy new particles, and naturalness is a criterion, not a law.

name: Gauge-coupling unification from RG running
summary: GUTs predict that the three SM gauge couplings meet at one scale. With SM coefficients, one-loop running misses a single meeting point; with MSSM coefficients the couplings meet near 2e16 GeV. That scale sets M_X and so the proton lifetime.

name: sin^2 theta_W = 3/8 at the unification scale
summary: Embedding SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) in SU(5) fixes the hypercharge normalization, g_1 = sqrt(5/3) g', so sin^2 theta_W = 3/8 at the unification scale. Running down to m_Z gives about 0.21 in the SM and close to the measured 0.2312 in the MSSM. The same embedding explains charge quantization (Q_d = Q_e/3).

name: QED to five loops in the lepton g-2
summary: The Schwinger term alpha/2pi began the precision testing of perturbative QFT. The QED part of the lepton anomalous moment is now known to tenth order (12,672 diagrams; Aoyama, Kinoshita, Nio). The electron g-2 therefore measures alpha at the sub-ppb level, while the muon g-2 uncertainty is dominated by non-perturbative hadronic loops.
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: Lattice HVP settles the muon g-2 comparison
summary: Hadronic vacuum polarization limits the SM prediction of a_mu. Lattice QCD (BMW 2020 onward) puts it above the e+e- dispersive value and closer to experiment, and the 2025 Theory Initiative update, which adopts lattice HVP, agrees with the final Fermilab result. The tension within the e+e- data (CMD-3 vs earlier experiments) is still unexplained.
map: a_\mu^{\rm HVP,LO}=\alpha^2\int_0^\infty dt\,K(t)\,G_{\rm em}(t)\ \ (\text{Euclidean vector correlator})
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: W mass: precision electroweak test and the CDF outlier
summary: The W mass follows from G_F, alpha and m_Z plus loop corrections Delta r that depend on the top and Higgs masses, which makes it a sharp new-physics probe (through the oblique T parameter). CDF's 2022 value sits about 7 sigma above the SM, but ATLAS (2024) and CMS (2024) agree with the SM, so CDF is treated as an unresolved outlier.

name: B anomalies as tests of lepton-flavor universality
summary: The lepton-universality ratios R_K(*) and R_D(*) in B decays were the flagship flavor anomalies. LHCb's 2022 reanalysis brought R_K(*) back to the SM, while R_D(*) is still about 3 sigma high. The case shows how flavor observables are judged against CKM-based predictions.
map: R_K=\frac{\mathcal B(B\to K\mu\mu)}{\mathcal B(B\to Kee)}\approx1\ ({\rm SM}),\ R_{D^{(*)}}=\frac{\mathcal B(B\to D^{(*)}\tau\nu)}{\mathcal B(B\to D^{(*)}\ell\nu)}

name: SUSY Higgs mass bound and the 125 GeV Higgs
summary: Boson-fermion loop cancellation removes the quadratic sensitivity of m_H^2, and the MSSM predicts a light Higgs with m_h <= m_Z |cos 2beta| at tree level. Reaching 125 GeV needs large stop loop corrections, from multi-TeV stops or maximal mixing, which is in tension with naturalness.

name: The LHC discovered and now measures the Higgs
summary: ATLAS and CMS discovered the 125 GeV Higgs in 2012, mainly via gluon fusion with H->gamma gamma and ZZ*->4l. The LHC now fits coupling modifiers kappa_i, which agree with the SM at the 5-10% level, and bounds the Higgs self-coupling through HH production.
map: \sigma\cdot{\rm BR}=\frac{\kappa_{\rm prod}^2\kappa_{\rm dec}^2}{\kappa_H^2}(\sigma\cdot{\rm BR})_{\rm SM};\ m_H\approx125\,{\rm GeV}

name: Soft-collinear EFT resums jet and event-shape logs
summary: SCET separates hard, collinear and soft modes with power counting lambda ~ p_T/Q and proves factorization theorems for jet observables. The RG evolution of each factor resums Sudakov double logarithms. It is used for thrust-based alpha_s fits, jet vetoes and jet mass.

name: Collinear factorization of amplitudes gives jets
summary: In soft and collinear limits, QCD amplitudes factorize into lower-point amplitudes times universal splitting functions, which makes infrared-safe jet rates computable (Sterman-Weinberg). Spinor-helicity and unitarity methods supply the multi-parton NLO and NNLO matrix elements behind multi-jet predictions.

name: Jets are the observable form of QCD partons
summary: Jets trace hard quarks and gluons through showering and hadronization. IR-safe algorithms such as anti-kT make them calculable in perturbative QCD, and jet rates, event shapes and 4-jet angular correlations measure alpha_s and the SU(3) color factors.

name: Normalizing flows for lattice gauge-field sampling
summary: Generative models from HEP machine learning, notably gauge-equivariant normalizing flows (Albergo, Kanwar, Shanahan and collaborators), are trained to sample lattice field configurations directly. The aim is to beat critical slowing down and topological freezing near the continuum limit. The same flow technology also drives phase-space sampling in event generators.
breaks: Flows are not yet competitive with HMC at physical QCD volumes, and their training cost grows steeply with lattice volume.

name: Parton showers and string hadronization model QCD
summary: Parton showers implement DGLAP evolution as a Markov chain with Sudakov no-emission probabilities. Hadronization uses either the Lund string, a linear confining flux tube that breaks by Schwinger-like q-qbar tunneling, or cluster models built on preconfinement.
breaks: Shower kernels follow from QCD factorization, but hadronization models are phenomenological, with parameters tuned to data rather than derived from QCD.

name: Weinberg operator: neutrino mass at dimension 5 in SMEFT
summary: Weinberg's (LH)(LH)/Lambda is the only dimension-5 operator built from SM fields, and it gives Majorana neutrino masses m_nu ~ v^2/Lambda. A mass near 0.05 eV then points to Lambda of 1e14-1e15 GeV. Seesaw types I-III are its tree-level UV completions, and neutrinoless double-beta decay tests its Delta L = 2.
map: \frac{c}{\Lambda}(\bar L^c\tilde H^*)(\tilde H^\dagger L)\ \to\ m_\nu\sim\frac{c\,v^2}{\Lambda},\ \text{type I: }\frac{c}{\Lambda}=\frac{y^2}{M_R}

name: MSW effect from charged-current forward scattering
summary: Coherent forward scattering of nu_e on electrons through W exchange adds a potential sqrt2 G_F n_e that changes the effective mixing; the flavor-universal Z-exchange term cancels for active neutrinos. The adiabatic MSW resonance explains the energy dependence of solar nu_e survival (SNO, Borexino) and gives long-baseline experiments sensitivity to the mass ordering.

name: PMNS and CKM: the same unitary mixing structure
summary: PMNS and CKM are both 3x3 unitary matrices that arise because mass and weak-interaction bases are misaligned. They share the parametrization (three angles and one Dirac phase, plus two Majorana phases for PMNS) and the Jarlskog invariant that controls CP violation. T2K, NOvA, DUNE and Hyper-K measure leptonic CP violation as the difference between nu_mu->nu_e and the antineutrino channel.
breaks: CKM angles are small and hierarchical while PMNS angles are large. Neutrino masses may be Majorana (seesaw) rather than Yukawa. Matter effects mimic a CP asymmetry in long-baseline data.

name: Gauge-anomaly cancellation fixes SM charges
summary: SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) is consistent only because gauge and mixed gauge-gravitational anomalies cancel within each generation, quarks against leptons. This requires N_c = 3 and the observed hypercharges, and it implies charge quantization. Witten's global SU(2) anomaly further requires an even number of doublets.

name: Axial anomaly: eta' mass and pi0 -> gamma gamma
summary: QCD has no ninth Goldstone boson because the anomaly and instantons break U(1)_A ('t Hooft). The Witten-Veneziano relation ties the eta' mass to the topological susceptibility, and the pi0 -> gamma gamma rate, fixed by the anomaly coefficient, confirms N_c = 3.

name: Fermi theory as the EFT of W exchange; SMEFT
summary: Fermi's four-fermion contact interaction is the low-energy limit of W exchange. It violates unitarity below about 1 TeV, which pointed to the weak scale. It is the template for SMEFT, where dimension-6 operators suppressed by Lambda^2 parametrize heavy new physics in electroweak and Higgs data.

name: Weak effective Hamiltonian and Wilson coefficients
summary: Flavor-changing decays are computed with a weak effective Hamiltonian obtained by integrating out W, Z and top. The operator product expansion separates short-distance Wilson coefficients, run from m_W to m_b with anomalous dimensions, from long-distance hadronic matrix elements. New physics shows up as shifts such as C_9 and C_10 in b -> s l l.

name: Chiral perturbation theory: EFT of QCD's Goldstones
summary: Spontaneous breaking of SU(3)_L x SU(3)_R to SU(3)_V makes the pions, kaons and eta pseudo-Goldstone bosons. Chiral perturbation theory (Weinberg, Gasser-Leutwyler) is the EFT that expands in p/Lambda_chi, with Lambda_chi of about 4 pi f_pi, roughly 1 GeV. Its leading term gives the GMOR relation.
map: \mathcal L_2=\frac{f^2}{4}{\rm Tr}(\partial_\mu U\partial^\mu U^\dagger)+\frac{f^2B}{2}{\rm Tr}(MU^\dagger+UM^\dagger)\Rightarrow m_\pi^2=B(m_u+m_d)

name: QCD is SU(3) Yang-Mills coupled to quarks
summary: QCD is the non-abelian Yang-Mills theory for SU(3) color. The general gauge-theory machinery supplies gluon self-interactions (from the structure constants), Faddeev-Popov ghosts and the sign of the one-loop beta function, as well as the confining phase and the theta vacua.

name: Lattice decay constants and form factors fix CKM
summary: Extracting CKM elements needs hadronic inputs that only lattice QCD supplies at percent precision: decay constants (f_K/f_pi, f_B), the kaon bag parameter B_K for epsilon_K, and B->D* and B->pi form factors for |V_cb| and |V_ub|. FLAG averages feed the unitarity-triangle fits, and the first-row unitarity deficit depends on these inputs.

name: Hadron spectrum and exotics from lattice QCD
summary: Lattice QCD reproduces the light hadron spectrum at the percent level (BMW 2008) and, with QED added, the neutron-proton mass splitting. Resonances and exotic candidates (X(3872), T_cc, hybrids) are studied by mapping finite-volume energy levels to scattering amplitudes with the Lüscher method.

name: Lattice QCD: QCD defined and solved non-perturbatively
summary: Wilson's lattice gauge action gives QCD a non-perturbative definition. Monte Carlo sampling of the Euclidean path integral then yields what perturbation theory cannot reach: the string tension and linear confining potential, hadron masses, quark masses and alpha_s.

name: Running Higgs quartic: electroweak vacuum metastability
summary: With m_h = 125 GeV and m_t of about 172.5 GeV, NNLO running drives the Higgs quartic lambda negative near 1e10-1e11 GeV. The electroweak vacuum is therefore metastable, with a lifetime far beyond the age of the universe. The conclusion depends sensitively on m_t and alpha_s.

name: Asymptotic freedom and dimensional transmutation
summary: The one-loop beta function of SU(3) with six flavors is negative, so alpha_s falls logarithmically at high Q (Gross-Wilczek and Politzer, 1973). The classically scale-free theory also generates the hadronic scale Lambda_QCD, a few hundred MeV, from a dimensionless coupling.

name: BBN as a probe of BSM physics
summary: Light-element abundances constrain extra relativistic species (N_eff), late-decaying particles, MeV-scale thermal dark matter and time-varying constants; BBN is the earliest laboratory for new physics.
sources: Sarkar (1996). "Big bang nucleosynthesis and physics beyond the standard model". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 59, 1493. [arXiv:hep-ph/9602260](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9602260)
Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Axion emission from nucleon bremsstrahlung
summary: Axion bounds from SN 1987A and neutron-star cooling rest on nuclear physics: NN bremsstrahlung rates, dense-matter EOS and superfluid gaps set how fast axions drain energy from hot nuclear matter.
sources: Caputo & Raffelt (2024). "Astrophysical Axion Bounds: The 2024 Edition". [arXiv:2401.13728](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.13728)

name: Nuclear transitions as dark-boson searches
summary: Excited-nucleus decays via internal pair creation can reveal light bosons; the ATOMKI 8Be/4He anomaly ('X17', ~17 MeV) prompted protophobic dark-photon models but is unconfirmed and contested (MEG II found no signal).
sources: Krasznahorkay et al. (2016). "Observation of Anomalous Internal Pair Creation in 8Be: A Possible Indication of a Light, Neutral Boson". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 042501. [arXiv:1504.01527](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.01527)

name: Baryon-to-photon ratio from BBN deuterium
summary: Baryogenesis must produce the eta_B that BBN measures from the primordial D/H ratio (and the CMB confirms); BBN is the earliest direct test of any baryogenesis model.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

Sakharov (1967). "Violation of CP invariance, C asymmetry, and baryon asymmetry of the universe". *Sov. Phys. Usp.* 34, 392. [doi:10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497](https://doi.org/10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497)

name: Nuclear structure factors for WIMP scattering
summary: Spin-dependent WIMP-nucleus cross sections need the proton and neutron spin content of each target nucleus, computed with the shell model; spin-independent rates need nuclear form factors and the coherent A^2 enhancement.
sources: Goodman & Witten (1985). "Detectability of Certain Dark Matter Candidates". *Phys. Rev. D* 31, 3059. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.31.3059](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.31.3059)

name: Proton radius puzzle as a precision anomaly
summary: The muonic-hydrogen proton radius disagreed with e-p data by ~5 sigma, a case study for judging precision anomalies (now largely resolved toward 0.84 fm); hadronic structure also limits the muon g-2 prediction.
sources: Pohl et al. (2010). "The size of the proton". *Nature* 466, 213. [doi:10.1038/nature09250](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09250)
Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: Neutron lifetime beam-bottle discrepancy
summary: Beam (~888 s) and bottle (~878 s) neutron lifetimes disagree by ~4 sigma; proposed dark decay channels are tested like other precision anomalies, and the lifetime also feeds BBN and V_ud.
sources: Fornal & Grinstein (2018). "Dark Matter Interpretation of the Neutron Decay Anomaly". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 191801. [arXiv:1801.01124](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.01124)

name: Proton structure as input to every LHC cross section
summary: LHC rates factorize into partonic cross sections convolved with PDFs measured in DIS; PDF uncertainties now limit precision Higgs and W-mass measurements.
sources: NNPDF Collaboration (2015). "Parton distributions for the LHC Run II". *JHEP* 04, 040. [arXiv:1410.8849](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.8849)

name: Next QCD collider after HERA and the LHC
summary: The EIC extends HERA's ep programme to polarized and nuclear beams; its small-x gluon and nuclear PDF measurements feed LHC and heavy-ion predictions, and it reuses collider accelerator and detector technology.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

name: DGLAP kernels are parton-shower kernels
summary: The splitting functions P(z) that evolve PDFs in ln mu^2 are the same kernels that generate collinear emissions in parton showers and jet evolution (space-like vs time-like evolution).
sources: Altarelli & Parisi (1977). "Asymptotic freedom in parton language". *Nucl. Phys. B* 126, 298. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4)
Sjöstrand et al. (2015). "An introduction to PYTHIA 8.2". *Comput. Phys. Commun.* 191, 159. [arXiv:1410.3012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.3012)

name: Jets as tomographic probes of the QGP
summary: IRC-safe jet algorithms, substructure and grooming developed for pp physics are applied in PbPb collisions; medium-induced radiation modifies the vacuum shower and the pp jets serve as the baseline for R_AA.
sources: Cacciari, Salam & Soyez (2008). "The anti-k_t jet clustering algorithm". *JHEP* 04, 063. [arXiv:0802.1189](https://arxiv.org/abs/0802.1189)

name: Geant4 transport for detectors and dose
summary: Geant4, built for HEP detector simulation, is a standard transport code for nuclear detector response and dosimetry, sharing the same cross-section libraries and showering physics.
sources: Agostinelli et al. (2003). "GEANT4—a simulation toolkit". *Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A* 506, 250. [doi:10.1016/S0168-9002(03)01368-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0168-9002(03)01368-8)

name: Collectivity and hadronization in small systems
summary: High-multiplicity pp collisions show flow-like correlations and strangeness enhancement once thought unique to nuclear collisions; event generators add core-corona or rope hadronization to describe them.
sources: Pierog et al. (2015). "EPOS LHC: Test of collective hadronization with data measured at the CERN Large Hadron Collider". *Phys. Rev. C* 92, 034906. [arXiv:1306.0121](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0121)
ALICE Collaboration (2017). "Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions". *Nature Phys.* 13, 535. [arXiv:1606.07424](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07424)

name: Quenching models built on vacuum parton showers
summary: Jet-quenching Monte Carlos (JEWEL, MARTINI, JETSCAPE) embed PYTHIA-type showers in an evolving medium, adding medium-induced splittings and recoils to the Sudakov evolution.
sources: Sjöstrand et al. (2015). "An introduction to PYTHIA 8.2". *Comput. Phys. Commun.* 191, 159. [arXiv:1410.3012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.3012)

name: Shared radiation-detector toolkit
summary: Applied nuclear physics (reactor instrumentation, dosimetry, isotope assay) and collider experiments use the same detector families and the same interaction physics; technology flows both ways.
sources: Particle Data Group (2024). "Review of Particle Physics". *Phys. Rev. D* 110, 030001. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001)

name: Same stopping-power physics and detector technologies
summary: Bethe-Bloch energy loss, scintillators, gas counters and silicon sensors are common to collider detectors and nuclear radiation detection; HEP trackers and calorimeters descend from nuclear counters and feed back into dosimetry instruments.
sources: Particle Data Group (2024). "Review of Particle Physics". *Phys. Rev. D* 110, 030001. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001)

name: Neutrino decoupling, N_eff and n/p freeze-out
summary: Weak n<->p conversions with neutrinos freeze out at T~0.8 MeV and set Y_p; the number of light neutrino species (N_eff) changes the expansion rate and hence the helium yield.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Pauli's neutrino and Fermi's beta decay
summary: The neutrino was invented to save energy conservation in beta decay and first detected via inverse beta decay at a reactor; beta spectra remain the key laboratory window on neutrino properties.
sources: Fermi (1934). "Versuch einer Theorie der β-Strahlen. I". *Z. Phys.* 88, 161. [doi:10.1007/BF01351864](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01351864)
Cowan, Reines et al. (1956). "Detection of the Free Neutrino: a Confirmation". *Science* 124, 103. [doi:10.1126/science.124.3212.103](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.124.3212.103)

name: Reactors as the strongest terrestrial antineutrino source
summary: Fission-fragment beta decays make ~6 antineutrinos per fission (~2x10^20 per second per GW_th); reactors gave the first neutrino detection, theta_13 (Daya Bay) and the JUNO ordering programme, and allow reactor monitoring.
sources: Cowan, Reines et al. (1956). "Detection of the Free Neutrino: a Confirmation". *Science* 124, 103. [doi:10.1126/science.124.3212.103](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.124.3212.103)
Daya Bay Collaboration (2012). "Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 108, 171803. [arXiv:1203.1669](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.1669)

name: Solar neutrinos measure pp-chain and CNO rates
summary: Solar neutrino fluxes are predicted from fusion S-factors (pp, 7Be(p,gamma)8B, 3He+4He) and measured by Borexino, SNO and Super-K, including the first CNO neutrinos; they test solar fusion and oscillations together.
sources: Adelberger et al. (2011). "Solar fusion cross sections. II. The pp chain and CNO cycles". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 195. [arXiv:1004.2318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2318)
Borexino Collaboration (2020). "Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun". *Nature* 587, 577. [arXiv:2006.15115](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15115)

name: Neutrino-nucleus cross sections and CEvNS
summary: Accelerator oscillation measurements are limited by neutrino-nucleus interaction models (quasi-elastic, meson production, final-state interactions); coherent elastic scattering grows as N^2 through the nuclear weak charge.
sources: Akimov et al. (2017). "Observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering". *Science* 357, 1123. [arXiv:1708.01294](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.01294)
Abe et al. (2026). "Constraining Neutrino Interaction Uncertainties for Neutrino Oscillation Measurements at the T2K Experiment". [arXiv:2606.14015](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14015)

name: Tritium endpoint and double-beta decay
summary: Absolute neutrino mass comes from the shape of the tritium beta spectrum near its endpoint (KATRIN), and Majorana nature from nuclear 0nubb decay; both are nuclear weak decays read as neutrino measurements.
sources: KATRIN Collaboration (2022). "Direct neutrino-mass measurement with sub-electronvolt sensitivity". *Nature Phys.* 18, 160. [arXiv:2105.08533](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.08533)
Avignone, Elliott & Engel (2008). "Double Beta Decay, Majorana Neutrinos, and Neutrino Mass". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 481. [arXiv:0708.1033](https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.1033)

name: Ab initio 0nubb matrix elements with uncertainties
summary: Turning a 0nubb half-life limit into m_bb needs |M^0nu|, which shell-model, QRPA and EDF calculations disagree on by 2-3x; ab initio methods with chiral EFT now give matrix elements with error bars, and two-body currents explain g_A quenching.
sources: Engel & Menéndez (2017). "Status and Future of Nuclear Matrix Elements for Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay: A Review". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 80, 046301. [arXiv:1610.06548](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.06548)
Belley et al. (2024). "Ab initio Uncertainty Quantification of Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay in Ge76". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 132, 182502. [arXiv:2308.15634](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.15634)
Gysbers et al. (2019). "Discrepancy between experimental and theoretical β-decay rates resolved from first principles". *Nature Phys.* 15, 428. [arXiv:1903.00047](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.00047)

name: Neutrino flavor conversion sets Y_e in r-process sites
summary: In supernovae and merger remnants, nu_e and anti-nu_e captures on nucleons set the electron fraction Y_e of ejecta; collective and fast flavor conversions can shift Y_e and so the r-process yields.
sources: Duan, Fuller & Qian (2010). "Collective Neutrino Oscillations". *Ann. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 60, 569. [arXiv:1001.2799](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.2799)

Arnould, Goriely & Takahashi (2007). "The r-process of stellar nucleosynthesis: Astrophysics and nuclear physics achievements and mysteries". *Phys. Rep.* 450, 97. [arXiv:0705.4512](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4512)

name: Reactor anomaly traced to fission beta spectra
summary: The reactor antineutrino anomaly came from converted fission beta spectra (Huber-Mueller); improved nuclear data and summation calculations removed much of it, and the 5 MeV bump is a nuclear-data feature, not oscillation.
sources: Mention et al. (2011). "The Reactor Antineutrino Anomaly". *Phys. Rev. D* 83, 073006. [arXiv:1101.2755](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2755)
Huber (2011). "On the determination of anti-neutrino spectra from nuclear reactors". *Phys. Rev. C* 84, 024617. [arXiv:1106.0687](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.0687)

name: Axial anomaly in the proton spin puzzle
summary: The flavor-singlet axial current is anomalous, so the quark-spin fraction Delta Sigma measured in polarized DIS mixes with gluon polarization; this anomaly is central to interpreting the EMC spin crisis.
sources: European Muon Collaboration (1988). "A measurement of the spin asymmetry and determination of the structure function g1 in deep inelastic muon-proton scattering". *Phys. Lett. B* 206, 364. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7)
Minamiguchi & Uji (2026). "Chiral anomaly and nucleon spin decomposition in the chiral quark soliton model". [arXiv:2609.25867](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25867)

name: Neutron EDM as the observable of theta
summary: The theta term is a P- and T-odd topological term that induces a neutron electric dipole moment; the measured bound gives |theta| < 10^-10, the strong-CP problem the axion solves.
sources: Crewther, Di Vecchia, Veneziano & Witten (1979). "Chiral Estimate of the Electric Dipole Moment of the Neutron in Quantum Chromodynamics". *Phys. Lett. B* 88, 123. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(79)90128-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(79)90128-X)
Abel et al. (2020). "Measurement of the Permanent Electric Dipole Moment of the Neutron". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 124, 081803. [arXiv:2001.11966](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.11966)

name: Topology and U(1)_A at the QCD transition
summary: Instanton-induced U(1)_A breaking controls the order of the chiral transition, the topological susceptibility sets the temperature-dependent axion mass, and sphaleron-driven chirality imbalance motivates chiral-magnetic-effect searches.
sources: Pisarski & Rennecke (2024). "Conjectures about the Chiral Phase Transition in QCD from Anomalous Multi-Instanton Interactions". [arXiv:2401.06130](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.06130)
Fukushima, Kharzeev & Warringa (2008). "The Chiral Magnetic Effect". *Phys. Rev. D* 78, 074033. [arXiv:0808.3382](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.3382)

name: Baryons as Skyrmions
summary: In the large-N chiral Lagrangian, baryons are topological solitons whose winding number is baryon number (the Wess-Zumino-Witten term fixes their fermionic statistics); Skyrmion models describe nucleons and light nuclei.
sources: Skyrme (1962). "A unified field theory of mesons and baryons". *Nucl. Phys.* 31, 556. [doi:10.1016/0029-5582(62)90775-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(62)90775-7)
Witten (1983). "Current algebra, baryons, and quark confinement". *Nucl. Phys. B* 223, 433. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(83)90064-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(83)90064-0)

name: Conformal plasmas as QGP benchmarks
summary: Strongly coupled conformal plasmas (N=4 SYM via holography) give eta/s=1/4pi, close to the QGP value; QCD's trace anomaly (epsilon-3P)/T^4 measures how far the real plasma is from conformal.
breaks: N=4 SYM is supersymmetric, conformal and large-N with no confinement, no chiral symmetry breaking and no running coupling; QCD is strongly non-conformal near T_c.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories from Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)
Boyd et al. (1996). "Thermodynamics of SU(3) lattice gauge theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 469, 419. [arXiv:hep-lat/9602007](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/9602007)

name: EFT organizes the nuclear many-body problem
summary: Nuclear structure theory is now built from a hierarchy of EFTs (chiral, pionless, halo), each with power counting and quantified truncation errors, as in particle-physics EFT.
sources: Hammer, König & van Kolck (2020). "Nuclear effective field theory: status and perspectives". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 92, 025004. [arXiv:1906.12122](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.12122)

name: Halo EFT and universality of weak binding
summary: Halo nuclei near the drip lines have a separation energy far below the core excitation scale, so a halo EFT with the core as a point particle applies, with universal (Efimov-like) features for two-neutron halos.
sources: Bedaque & van Kolck (2002). "Effective field theory for few-nucleon systems". *Ann. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 52, 339. [arXiv:nucl-th/0203055](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0203055)
Hammer, König & van Kolck (2020). "Nuclear effective field theory: status and perspectives". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 92, 025004. [arXiv:1906.12122](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.12122)

name: Chiral EFT as Weinberg's power counting for nuclei
summary: Weinberg's phenomenological-Lagrangian program (chiral perturbation theory) was carried into nuclear physics as chiral EFT, organizing nucleon-nucleon and three-nucleon forces in powers of Q/Lambda_chi.
sources: Weinberg (1979). "Phenomenological Lagrangians". *Physica A* 96, 327. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1)
Weinberg (1990). "Nuclear forces from chiral lagrangians". *Phys. Lett. B* 251, 288. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3)
Epelbaum, Hammer & Meißner (2009). "Modern theory of nuclear forces". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1773. [arXiv:0811.1338](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.1338)

name: Lattice QCD for g_A, spin and gravitational form factors
summary: Lattice QCD computes the nucleon axial charge, quark and gluon spin and orbital contributions, and gravitational form factors (pressure and shear distributions) from first principles.
sources: Hackett et al. (2024). "Gravitational Form Factors of the Proton from Lattice QCD". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 132, 251904. [arXiv:2310.08484](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08484)

name: Large-momentum effective theory puts PDFs on the lattice
summary: Light-cone PDFs cannot be computed in Euclidean time, but equal-time quasi-PDFs in a highly boosted nucleon can, and are matched to PDFs perturbatively (LaMET); lattice results now complement global fits.
sources: Ji (2013). "Parton Physics on a Euclidean Lattice". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 110, 262002. [arXiv:1305.1539](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.1539)

name: Lattice QCD finds the crossover at T_c~156 MeV
summary: Euclidean lattice Monte Carlo establishes that the physical-mass QCD transition at mu_B=0 is a crossover and computes the equation of state and susceptibilities used to search for a critical point; the sign problem blocks large mu_B.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)
Borsanyi et al. (2010). "Is there still any T_c mystery in lattice QCD? Results with physical masses in the continuum limit III". *JHEP* 09, 073. [arXiv:1005.3508](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.3508)

name: Lattice equation of state drives QGP hydrodynamics
summary: Lattice QCD thermodynamics provides the QGP equation of state, speed of sound and trace anomaly used as input to relativistic hydrodynamic simulations of heavy-ion collisions.
sources: Boyd et al. (1996). "Thermodynamics of SU(3) lattice gauge theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 469, 419. [arXiv:hep-lat/9602007](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/9602007)
Borsanyi et al. (2010). "Is there still any T_c mystery in lattice QCD? Results with physical masses in the continuum limit III". *JHEP* 09, 073. [arXiv:1005.3508](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.3508)

name: Nuclear lattice EFT reuses lattice Monte Carlo
summary: Nuclear lattice EFT discretizes chiral-EFT nucleons on a Euclidean space-time lattice and samples auxiliary fields by Monte Carlo, inheriting lattice-QCD algorithms and the fermion sign problem.
sources: Lee (2009). "Lattice simulations for few- and many-body systems". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 63, 117. [arXiv:0804.3501](https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.3501)

name: Lattice QCD computes nucleon-nucleon interactions
summary: Lattice QCD extracts two-baryon scattering from finite-volume energy levels (Luscher's method) and fixes chiral-EFT low-energy constants, connecting nuclear forces to QCD.
sources: Beane, Detmold, Orginos & Savage (2011). "Nuclear Physics from Lattice QCD". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 66, 1. [arXiv:1004.2935](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2935)

name: SRG/IMSRG as Wilsonian RG for nuclei
summary: Similarity renormalization group evolution decouples high- and low-momentum modes of nuclear Hamiltonians, the nuclear realization of Wilson's integrating-out; induced many-body forces play the role of generated irrelevant operators.
sources: Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)
Bogner, Furnstahl & Schwenk (2010). "From low-momentum interactions to nuclear structure". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 65, 94. [arXiv:0912.3688](https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.3688)
He & Stroberg (2024). "Factorized approximation to the in-medium similarity renormalization group IMSRG(3)". [arXiv:2405.19594](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19594)

name: Octupole-deformed nuclei amplify T violation
summary: Nuclear Schiff moments induced by CP-odd nucleon interactions are enhanced by orders of magnitude in octupole-deformed nuclei with parity doublets (225Ra, 227Ac), making atomic EDM searches sensitive probes of hadronic CP violation.

name: Both Standard Model transitions are crossovers
summary: Lattice studies show that at physical masses the electroweak transition (m_h=125 GeV) and the QCD transition are both smooth crossovers, which removes the SM's own departure from equilibrium for baryogenesis and for primordial relics.
sources: Kajantie, Laine, Rummukainen & Shaposhnikov (1996). "Is there a hot electroweak phase transition at m_H ≳ m_W?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 77, 2887. [arXiv:hep-ph/9605288](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9605288)

Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)

name: Z-boson exchange measures the neutron skin
summary: Parity-violating electron scattering couples to the weak charge, which is carried mostly by neutrons (Q_W^p ~ 1-4 sin^2 theta_W ~ 0.07); PREX-II's 208Pb neutron skin constrains the symmetry-energy slope L and neutron-star radii.
sources: PREX Collaboration (2021). "Accurate Determination of the Neutron Skin Thickness of 208Pb through Parity-Violation in Electron Scattering". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 126, 172502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.126.172502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.126.172502)
